title: The Future of Knowledge Assistants: Jerry Liu
talk_summary: Jerry Liu of LlamaIndex argues that naive RAG is insufficient and lays out a three-step progression: better data parsing/retrieval, agentic single-agent query flows (function calling, planning, memory), and multi-agent task solvers. He then pitches Llama Agents, an alpha framework representing each agent as a microservice communicating via a central API/control plane, inspired by Kubernetes-style resource allocation.

takeaways.technique: Specialist agents with small tool sets instead of one agent with many tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Split work so each agent operates over only 5-10 tools rather than one agent holding a thousand tools, which he says current models fail at; specialists are more reliable and can use weaker/faster models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of having you know a single agent access like a thousand tools you could potentially have each agent operate over like you know 5 to 10 tool
takeaways.numbers: 5-10 tools per agent vs ~1000 for a single agent

takeaways.technique: Weaker/faster models enabled by narrower agent scope
takeaways.what_they_do: Because each specialist agent has fewer tools and a focused task, it can be served by a cheaper, lower-latency model instead of a frontier model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: have each agent operate over like you know 5 to 10 tool and therefore use a weaker and faster model and so there are actually potential cost and latency savings

takeaways.technique: Agents as microservices behind a central control plane
takeaways.what_they_do: Represent each agent as a separate deployable service that communicates via a message queue/API, with orchestration either explicit (defined flows) or implicit (an LLM orchestrator delegating tasks), borrowing from Kubernetes-style resource allocators.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every agent is just represented as a separate service um you can write the agents however you want

takeaways.technique: Parallel copies of the same agent for throughput
takeaways.what_they_do: Run multiple instances of the same agent to parallelize independent tasks and finish faster.
takeaways.evidence_quote: by being able to have you know multiple copies of even like the same allim agent you're able to paralyze a bunch of tasks

takeaways.what_they_do: Use proper document parsers that preserve spatial/table structure instead of naive text extraction, because collapsed tables cause hallucinations; good parsing alone improves answer accuracy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: even good parsing itself can improve performance right even without advanced indexing retrieval good parsing helps to reduce hallucinations

takeaways.what_they_do: Distinguishes unconstrained agent-to-agent flows from explicitly injecting constraints/forcing an agent to operate a certain way given an input; flags reliability as the production challenge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: actually being able to inject some sort of strengths between the agents you're basically explicitly forcing an agent to operate in a certain way given a certain input
